s0474: Adult audience for Dinobutin: a separate test doesn’t look worthwhile
s0475: An adult needs 10–20 ml of gel per dose, 3 times a day (100–200 mg). That is 2–4 measuring spoons per dose and 6–12 spoons a day. A 100 g tube lasts about 1.5–3 days.
s0476: A 28-day course would cost roughly **RUB 7–14K**, several times more than tablet alternatives.
s0478: Trimebutine tablets are simpler and more familiar: a 200 mg single dose is one tablet (usually 2–3 times a day).
s0479: Extended-release forms exist: Trimedat Forte 300 mg — 1 tablet twice a day.
s0480: The Russian market confirms the trend: tablets are the most popular form and account for **46.5% of spending** on medicines.
s0482: There are few organic adult reviews of Dinobutin. Main signal — doubts about convenience and course cost:
s0483: “with IBS you need several tubes. basically this form is just for kids”
s0484: Adults tend to choose tablets for simplicity: one tablet per dose, no spoons, no taste, no measuring.
s0486: Taken together, these factors suggest a separate adult segment test makes little sense. A search demand check confirmed it: queries about dysphagia, difficulty swallowing or a liquid form of trimebutine are either almost absent or give only **50–100 queries a month**. That volume is too small to expect noticeable reach or a reliable test result.
